issue_paraphrase: A template that declares a required block and places a statement inside it - for example a nested child block or a conditional - fails to compile, but instead of reporting the intended template-syntax error, the parser crashes with an internal AttributeError about an object lacking a 'nodes' attribute and dumps a confusing Python traceback. Required blocks containing only whitespace or comments compile fine, and blocks containing literal text already produce the intended clear error; the crash is specific to statement content. The friendly message the project intends for this situation ('Required blocks can only contain comments or whitespace') is never shown to the user.
fix_summary: The pre-fix check iterated child.nodes of every body statement, assuming every node has a .nodes attribute (true only for Output/TemplateData); statement nodes such as If or Block raised AttributeError before the intended failure. The fix verifies each body node is an Output node (and that all its TemplateData leaves are whitespace) before raising TemplateSyntaxError('Required blocks can only contain comments or whitespace'), and rewrites the regression test to cover empty/blank accepted cases and text/nested-block/if rejected cases. Bug present since required blocks were introduced (2020-06-10, commit 8da77f97).
notes: Fully offline, no network, ~0.05 s for the golden test. Only pytest + jinja2(+markupsafe) needed. Do not pint to pytest>=8: era tests use the removed callable form of pytest.raises (does not affect this specific golden test, but affects the surrounding file at this era). Full suite at the fix commit: 874 passed in ~2 s (with pytest 7.4.3 + trio + pytest-timeout).

issue_paraphrase: When an application renders a template in async mode and consumes its output incrementally - streaming a page, using include, or rendering through template inheritance - the underlying async generators are never closed when iteration stops early. Event-loop runtimes that actively police resource cleanup then report ResourceWarning diagnostics such as 'Async generator was garbage collected before it had been exhausted', and some libraries turn those warnings into failures, so perfectly normal streaming code starts crashing. The code generated for a template yields from nested async generators (parent/child templates, includes, block calls) but never calls aclose on them when the consumer stops reading, and the helper that adapts iterators to async iteration adds another unclosed generator layer of its own.
fix_summary: auto_aiter is no longer an async-generator function: for async iterables it returns iterable.__aiter__() and for sync iterables it returns a tiny _IteratorToAsyncIterator wrapper, so no extra generator layer exists to leak. Compiled template code that yields from a parent template's root render function, from an included/extended template's root render function, or from a block call now wraps the smart for-loop in try/finally that awaits agen.aclose() (or calls gen.close() in sync mode). Tests were reworked to run under both asyncio and trio runners via a parametrized run_async_fn fixture, and the new aclose regression tests exercise generate_async with explicit early stop + aclose.
notes: Golden tests are deterministic here: at the parent all four trio params failed reproducibly; at the fix all 8 pass. The failure surfaces during pytest teardown as pluggy.PluggyTeardownRaisedWarning wrapping trio's ResourceWarning, so the pytest exit code is non-zero at parent. No network needed. Full suite at fix commit: 874 passed in ~2 s at 1 CPU. Prefer running the four tests as a group (they cover include/extends/self-block and a plain for-loop).

issue_paraphrase: Templates that test membership against a variable that is not defined, such as checking whether a key or label appears in a possibly-missing object, now abort rendering with an UndefinedError instead of simply evaluating the membership test to false as they did in the previous major version. The regression breaks templates that probe optional data by membership: rendering stops with a traceback even though the template author clearly intended the undefined value to behave as an empty/falsy container. Only templates using the default undefined type are affected; users who opted into strict-undefined mode still expect the operation to raise.
fix_summary: Jinja 2.x made 'x in undefined' evaluate to False (default Undefined delegates to the base object's membership behavior); the 3.0 development cycle wired __contains__ to _fail_with_undefined_error (commit 609bcb08, 2020-05-09). This fix reverts that: Undefined.__contains__ no longer raises, so 'in' yields False, while StrictUndefined keeps __contains__ = _fail_with_undefined_error. Regression test updated to assert '{{ 'foo' in missing }}' renders 'False' for the default undefined and still raises for strict undefined.
notes: Trivial two-line source change (src delta 2 lines, the smallest of the three entries) but a genuine user-visible 3.0 regression with the project's own regression test; flag if pool reviewers prefer >=4-line deltas. Offline, no network, golden test runs in <0.1 s.
